doc.title: Frank Wess — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: NEA Jazz Masters events and old friends Snooky Young and Gerald Wilson
summary: Wess describes the NEA Jazz Masters ceremonies as a reunion of friends known since 1940, praising Gerald Wilson.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you, in the next couple of days we have all of these NEA Jazz Masters events going on and you were named an NEA Jazz Master in 2007. This will be the third year you have been involved in these activities. Can you talk a little bit about, you know, the experience of being involved in this circle of jazz legends?

They have quite a program at the time that they have the awards and ceremony. You know, it takes up the whole day or so, doing that. It’s nice, you get…I think last year Snooky Young got an award and Gerald Wilson and I presented. Like, you know, that was nice. We’ve all known each other since 1940, you know what I mean? It’s like old friends, you get to know them.
Yeah, that was a great presentation; you guys were funny.
Gerald, he remembers everything and he was acting like he was 19-years old, it was unbelievable. He’s 90 something. I think Snooks is about 92.
He is remarkable and he teachers, and he has some absolutely astounding number in his class. I mean, hundreds and hundreds of students in his one lecture class.
Gerald Wilson, he’s something else, he really is.
